Notes

The scoring rule

The rules come from FiveThirtyEight's old NFL forecasting game, as later recreated by Lee Sharpe. Each game is worth 25 − 100 × (P − R)² points, where P is the probability given to the home team and R is whether it won. A coin flip scores nothing. Being certain and right is worth 25 - being certain and wrong costs 75.

Live and retrodiction

2026 is live. Every forecast is read back from that Tuesday's archive, written before kickoff, and the market is the price on file next to it.

Every season before that is retrodiction - today's model applied backwards to seasons already played. The timing inside a season is honest, since a week 10 game is forecast from week 9 ratings, but the model was built knowing how those seasons ended. The market there is the closing spread run through the same margin-to-probability step the models use. Compare seasons within a label, not across them.

Regular season only

Regular season only, for now. LOWFI rates teams from regular-season games, so it has no opinion about a divisional round game and none are scored here. That leaves out exactly the games the rules weight most heavily - a Super Bowl call is worth five times a week 3 one.
